about.title: About PDF to Word Notes
description: This page currently explains common expectations and limitations in a PDF to Word workflow rather than presenting a fully launched conversion product.
PDF to Word output often requires manual review, especially when the source file contains complex layout, tables, scanned pages, or mixed fonts.
The interactive version is not part of the featured public surface until implementation details, scope limits, and policy wording are reviewed together.

howTo.title: How to Use This Review Note

steps.title: Check the source document
steps.description: Decide whether the PDF is text-based, scanned, heavily formatted, or built from images before expecting a clean editable result.

steps.title: Set realistic expectations
steps.description: Use this page to understand where layout drift, OCR errors, table issues, or font substitution are common.

steps.title: Choose the right workflow
steps.description: If you only need to read, annotate, or extract a small section, a full Word conversion may not be the best path.

steps.title: Verify the result independently
steps.description: Before sharing or acting on converted text, compare the output with the original PDF line by line where accuracy matters.

tips: Scanned PDFs often need extra review because OCR mistakes are common.
Tables, headers, footers, and multi-column layouts are frequent sources of formatting drift.
For legal, academic, or contractual material, always verify the converted document manually.

faq.q: Why can PDF to Word output still need manual cleanup?
faq.a: PDF files are built for fixed presentation, not for easy reconstruction into editable document structure. Layout, fonts, tables, and scanned text can all introduce errors.

faq.q: Are scanned PDFs harder to convert?
faq.a: Yes. Scanned pages often depend on OCR, which can misread characters, spacing, or structure, especially in low-quality scans.

faq.q: Why is this page not shown as a complete public tool?
faq.a: The public site only promotes file workflows after implementation details, limits, and policy wording are reviewed together.

faq.q: When should I verify the converted document manually?
faq.a: Always verify manually when formatting, quoted text, figures, legal language, academic citations, or contractual terms matter.
